text:
alex: Hey, noticing a weird SSE subscription drift in prod since ~03:40 UTC. active_subscriptions for /v1/stream/resp keeps climbing, clients don't seem to re-subscribe. cc @maya

maya: Any logs or a dashboard link?

alex: Dash: /dash/streams -> active_subscriptions (us-west) rising steadily, orphaned-sse-count > 500. Logs show a lot of 204s from the proxy during idle windows.

alex: Snippet from proxy logs:
```
2026-03-05T03:41:12Z proxy INFO upstream -> client: 204 No Content (keepalive)
2026-03-05T03:41:12Z proxy DEBUG stream ended cleanly (code=204) conn=abc123
2026-03-05T03:41:12Z client WARN connection closed, client lib not resubscribing
```

maya: 204 as keepalive is suspicious. Many SSE/eventsource polyfills treat 204 as terminal (success) and won't reconnect. We should be sending a ping comment or 200 with an SSE comment.

martin: We got an automated alert earlier from stream-health-bot: orphaned-sse-count > 1000 for 10m. samp conn ids included.

sre-bot: [automated] alert: orphaned-sse-count high (us-west). sample connection: abc123, host: proxy-12

elaine: Reminder: last week's platform change swapped keepalive behavior to rely on proxy defaults. Might be the culprit. We should decide hotfix vs rollback.

alex: I can reproduce locally with curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -> server returns HTTP/1.1 204 after idle and eventsource polyfills close the stream (no reconnect). Repro steps in a gist: https://git.company/infra/stream-repro (private).

maya: Proposed short-term fix: translate upstream idle 204 -> 200 and inject a single SSE comment line (`:\n\n`) so clients see data and keep waiting. Longer term: fix upstream to emit `:\n` pings or explicit `event: ping` frames.

martin: Also need better telemetry: a metric `sse_terminated_by_status` to know how many end with 204/200/500. Current orphaned-sse alert aggregates too coarsely.

elaine: UX/Docs: add a Streaming section in Console docs about keepalive semantics and supported client behaviors; include recommended client library versions. I'll draft.

alex: Quick mitigation plan: patch proxy to convert 204->200 + `:\n\n` for idle keepalive. I'll open PR and feature-flag the behavior.

maya: Can we canary the proxy change to a small subset (dedicated region) before global rollout? Put a flag keyed by region.

martin: Agree. We'll roll to 2 canary nodes in us-west tonight, monitor orphaned-sse-count and active_subscriptions. If we don't see drop in 10m windows, revert.

elaine: I'll create a support template for customers on older clients and link to the doc change.

alex: PR created: https://git.company/infra/proxy/pull/542 (patch: translate 204->200 & inject `:\n`)

maya: After patch merges, add an explicit test in e2e that simulates upstream idle 204 and ensures client libraries still maintain connection.

martin: For postmortem, capture client lib versions that fail on 204 and the timeline from deploy->alert->mitigation. Also include dashboard panel for `sse_terminated_by_status`.

alex: ack. I'll add the test and a short note in the PR describing the compatibility issue.

elaine: Nice work. Once canary is healthy, we should include a small Console banner for customers about the fix and mention which clients were impacted. :thumbsup:

maya: Monitoring runbook: watch active_subscriptions (5m), orphaned-sse-count (1m), and error-rate for /v1/stream/resp. Set temporary alert threshold to 300 for 5m during rollout.

martin: I'll schedule the canary window at 01:00 UTC to hit low traffic. Will update this thread when started.

alex: Thanks. I'll follow up with PR updates and the local repro steps.
